proposal: If the prior administration let TikTok keep operating, a new administration should ban the app on national security grounds. The FCC should also keep its Covered List current, close the loophole that lets barred Chinese carriers serve data centers, publish a list of licensees with more than 10 percent foreign adversary government ownership, fully fund rip-and-replace, and pursue clean standards and anti-China AI measures.

status_summary: The TikTok element went a different way from the recommendation: executive orders delayed enforcement of the 2024 divest-or-ban law, an order published 2025-09-30 described a qualified divestiture process, and a U.S. joint venture deal closed on 2026-01-22 (Politico), so the app was not banned. The FCC elements have advanced. On 2025-12-22 the FCC's Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau added to the Covered List all foreign-produced drones and drone critical components and the communications and video surveillance equipment listed in Section 1709 of the FY2025 defense law, based on an executive branch interagency determination dated 2025-12-21; on 2026-07-06 FCC bureaus barred continued import and marketing of previously authorized equipment added to the list in 2024 or earlier. A final rule published 2025-11-25 bars authorizing devices with covered modular transmitters, and a final rule published 2026-09-11 closes a component-part loophole for Covered List entities. A proposal published 2026-05-08 would exclude Covered List entities from blanket domestic Section 214 authority and tentatively treats interconnection with them, including at data centers, as unreasonable, which tracks the chapter's data-center loophole point but is not final. A final rule published 2026-04-10 (effective 2026-06-09) requires licensees to attest whether they are foreign adversary controlled and treats a holder of 10 percent or more as having control power; the compliance date is still to be announced and the text read does not provide for a public list of such licensees, which the chapter recommends. On rip-and-replace, Congress authorized the FCC to borrow $3.08 billion in December 2024, before the period tracked, and the FCC announced in April 2025 that it had the funds. A clean standards initiative and an AI plan were not verified.

timeline.event: Presidential document published as Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security: it summarizes the executive orders that delayed enforcement of the divest-or-ban law and describes the qualified divestiture process that could lift the law's prohibitions.
FCC final rule bars authorizing devices that contain covered modular transmitters and adds a procedure to limit prior authorizations of covered equipment.

FCC bureau adds all foreign-produced drones and drone critical components, and Section 1709 communications and video surveillance equipment, to the Covered List after an interagency determination dated 2025-12-21 (as described in a later FCC notice).

TikTok announces that a U.S. joint venture deal valued at $14 billion has closed; Silver Lake, MGX and Oracle each hold 15 percent and the parent company keeps a stake of nearly 20 percent (Politico, republished by Yahoo Finance).

FCC final rule requires holders of FCC licenses and authorizations to attest whether they are owned or controlled by a foreign adversary and to disclose details if so; effective 2026-06-09, with compliance dates to be announced; a holder of 10 percent or more is presumed to hold control power.
FCC proposed rule would exclude Covered List entities from blanket domestic Section 214 authority and tentatively find interconnection with them, including at data centers, unreasonable.
FCC bureaus bar the continued import and marketing of previously authorized equipment added to the Covered List in 2024 or earlier, acting through a public notice under rule 2.939.
FCC final rule closes a component-part loophole for Covered List entities, requires full certification for their modifications, and requires online marketplaces to display FCC IDs.

title: Ban TikTok and expand FCC restrictions on Chinese-linked equipment and carriers
uncertainties: This record combines a TikTok element that diverged from the recommendation with FCC elements that are partly on track, and the 45 progress figure is a judgment across them. The Covered List page on fcc.gov is an old cached copy, so additions were read from a later FCC notice rather than the list itself. The data-center point rests on the proposal's description in the earlier review, since the proposal text was not re-read. The attestation rule's text was read only to character 100,000 of about 139,000, so a public-list provision later in the document cannot be ruled out. The rip-and-replace funding source is trade press; the borrowing authority date (December 2024) predates the inauguration and disbursement progress was not found. The terms of the TikTok joint venture were taken from a Politico report, not a primary document.
